title: The Karnataka Illegal Mining Scam
dek: A mining baron and state minister was accused of running an illegal iron-ore empire worth thousands of crores. After a 13-year trial, the verdict finally came in 2025 — guilty, seven years, and a fine of exactly ₹10,000.

heroStat.label: loss to the exchequer proven at trial, from illegal mining between 2007 and 2009

promise.quote: Iron ore mining leases in Karnataka's Bellary region will be operated within their sanctioned boundaries, with royalties and taxes paid honestly to the state.
promise.madeBy: Obulapuram Mining Company (OMC) and associated lease-holders, under G. Janardhana Reddy
promise.role: Private mining company; Reddy also served as a Karnataka state minister
promise.context: Reddy and associates were accused of mining well beyond sanctioned lease boundaries and exporting ore without proper royalty payments, as part of what investigators described as a broader ₹16,500 crore illegal mining scandal across the Bellary region.

target.description: Mining conducted strictly within sanctioned lease boundaries, with royalties and export duties paid honestly to the state exchequer.
target.standard: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act and state mining lease conditions.

reality.description: After a 13-year trial, a CBI court in Hyderabad convicted G. Janardhana Reddy and three others — OMC managing director B.V. Srinivasa Reddy, former Andhra Pradesh mines department official V.D. Rajagopal, and Reddy's personal assistant Mehfaz Ali Khan — on 6 May 2025 in the Obulapuram Mining Company case, finding they had caused a proven loss of ₹884 crore to the exchequer through illegal mining between 2007 and 2009. All four were sentenced to seven years' imprisonment and fined ₹10,000 each.

gap.metricLabel: Broader alleged scale of the Bellary mining scandal vs. the loss proven in this specific conviction
gap.note: The wider ₹16,500 crore figure describes the broader Bellary-region illegal mining scandal Reddy was associated with; the ₹884 crore figure is what was specifically proven in this one court case (the OMC case) after a full trial, and this investigation treats the proven figure as the more reliable of the two.

timeline.label: Illegal mining period begins
timeline.detail: OMC allegedly begins mining beyond its sanctioned lease boundaries.

timeline.label: Reddy taken into custody
timeline.detail: He is arrested and later brought to Bangalore.

timeline.label: Convictions and sentencing
timeline.detail: A CBI court convicts and sentences four people to seven years' imprisonment each in the OMC case.

legalStatus.summary: This is a final, adjudicated criminal conviction reached after a 13-year trial, one of the more clearly resolved cases on this site.

keyIndividuals.name: G. Janardhana Reddy
keyIndividuals.role: Former Karnataka state minister; promoter, Obulapuram Mining Company
keyIndividuals.outcome: Convicted 6 May 2025 and sentenced to seven years' imprisonment and a ₹10,000 fine, after a 13-year trial.

verdict.summary: This is a rare case on this site with a completed criminal trial and a specific, court-proven loss figure. It also illustrates how long Indian trials for large corruption cases can take — 13 years from the alleged conduct's exposure to a verdict — and how the eventual proven loss (₹884 crore) can differ substantially from the much larger figure attached to the broader scandal in public memory (₹16,500 crore).
verdict.reasoning: The conviction, sentence, and specific loss figure are all matters of court record from a concluded trial, reported consistently across sources.

incomplete: This is a stub entry. Whether Reddy or the other convicted individuals have filed appeals, and the status of any such appeal, has not been researched.
This case is one of several separate mining-related proceedings Reddy has faced; this entry covers only the OMC conviction and does not catalogue his other cases.
